entities.summary:
The Battle of al-Qadisiyyah, fought from November 19 to 22, 636 AD, was a pivotal event in world history, marking a decisive victory for the Rashidun Caliphate over the Sasanian Empire. This battle took place in Al-Qādisiyyah, modern-day Iraq, and had profound implications for the spread of Islam, the fate of the Middle East, and the trajectory of global politics. The Rashidun forces, led by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, achieved a crushing defeat over the Sasanians, led by Rustam Farrukhzad, resulting in the death of thousands of Sasanian soldiers and the eventual collapse of the Sasanian Empire. The consequences of this battle were far-reaching, shaping the course of Islamic history, the rise of the Umayyad Caliphate, and the spread of Islam into the Middle East and beyond.

The Battle of al-Qadisiyyah was a turning point in the Arab conquest of Persia, marking the beginning of the end of the Sasanian Empire. The Rashidun forces, fueled by their faith and driven by strategic leadership, were able to overcome the valiant defense of the Sasanian army. The outcome of this battle was a testament to the military prowess and organizational skills of the Rashidun forces, who were able to adapt to the challenging terrain and successfully execute their battle plan. The defeat of the Sasanian Empire at the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah had significant implications for the regional balance of power, paving the way for the rise of the Umayyad Caliphate and the spread of Islam into the Middle East and beyond.
